ops.old: In performance year 2024, 476 ACOs generated $6.6 billion in total gross savings relative to benchmarks. After accounting for $4.1 billion paid out as shared savings to ACOs, Medicare retained $2.4 billion in net savings—the largest in program history. The per-capita net savings were $241 per attributed beneficiary, up from $207 in 2023. Since the program's inception, ACOs have generated $35 billion in gross savings and $13.6 billion in net savings to Medicare.
ops.new: In performance year 2024, 476 ACOs saved $651 per assigned beneficiary relative to their benchmarks (gross), up from $515 in 2023. After $4.1 billion in performance payments to ACOs, Medicare saved $2.5 billion — $245 per beneficiary, up from $207 — the highest savings since the program began.
ops.claim: PY2024: $6.6B gross, $2.4B net, $241 per capita; cumulative $35B gross / $13.6B net since inception
ops.sources: CMS fact sheet "MSSP ACOs Updated Performance Year 2024 Financial and Quality Results" (2025-09-29): 476 ACOs; 75% earning $4.1B; Medicare saved $2.5B; $245 net / $651 gross per capita (vs $207/$515 in 2023); low-revenue $319 vs high-revenue $180; primary-care-heavy $403 vs $224
ops.note: Net and per-capita figures corrected to CMS's updated fact sheet; total-gross and cumulative figures do not appear in CMS sources and were dropped.

ops.old: The CBO used counterfactual control groups—comparable providers not participating in ACOs—to estimate how much ACO participation actually reduced spending relative to what would have occurred otherwise. The CBO found "mixed results" across models, with some ACO programs achieving small net savings and others showing small net costs when measured against counterfactuals.
ops.new: Rather than relying on CMS's benchmark comparisons, the CBO reviewed research that estimates savings against comparison groups of non-ACO providers. That research suggests ACOs have produced modest gross savings, and that net savings to Medicare — after shared-savings payments — have been smaller and less certain than benchmark-based figures imply.
ops.claim: CBO used its own counterfactual control groups and found "mixed results" across models
ops.sources: CBO, "Medicare Accountable Care Organizations: Past Performance and Future Directions" (2024-04-16, cbo.gov/publication/60213) — a review of research: greater savings associated with ACOs led by independent physician groups, with a larger share of primary care providers, and with baseline spending above the regional average
ops.note: CBO reviewed others' research; the quoted phrase could not be found.

ops.old: The CBO's more positive findings were concentrated in specific ACO types: physician-led ACOs, ACOs with higher primary care concentration, ACOs that accepted more financial risk (downside-risk tracks), and ACOs in their earlier agreement periods. These characteristics align with the theoretical model of how ACOs should work—primary care-driven coordination, strong financial incentives, and early-stage enthusiasm for change.
ops.new: The CBO found greater savings associated with specific ACO types: ACOs led by independent physician groups, ACOs with a larger proportion of primary care providers, and ACOs whose baseline spending was higher than their regional average. These characteristics align with the theoretical model of how ACOs should work — primary care-driven coordination and room to reduce excess spending.

ops.old: The NGACO model generated $667 million in gross savings across performance years 2016 to 2019. However, after accounting for $909 million in shared savings and other payouts to risk-bearing ACOs, the NGACO model was associated with $243 million in net losses to Medicare over four performance years. CMS terminated the NGACO model after performance year 2021 on these grounds.
ops.new: Measured against benchmarks, CMS reported that Next Generation ACOs produced net savings to Medicare of about $62 million in 2016, $185 million in 2018 and $204 million in 2019, after shared savings and losses. The model ended as scheduled after an extension through 2021 for the COVID-19 public health emergency, and its features carried into the Global and Professional Direct Contracting model and then ACO REACH.
ops.claim: NGACO $667M gross, $909M payouts, $243M net losses (2016-2019); CMS terminated NGACO on those grounds
ops.sources: CMS/NORC NGACO first-year results (2016: ~$62M net savings, AHA News 2018-08-29); CMS PY2018/PY2019 NGACO results via Managed Healthcare Executive and NAACOS ($406M/$185M 2018; $559M/$204M 2019); NGACO model page (extended through 2021)
